findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above the safe maximum cold holding temperature in the 2-door drawer cooler under the grill:
1. Gyro meat (60.9F with probe)
2. Two containers of raw hamburger (60.0F and 62.3F with probe
3. Sliced cheese (63.4F with probe)
4. BBQ Pork (56.8F with probe)
The PIC was informed and chose to discard all TCS foods in the cooler. The PIC investigated the cooler further and discovered that the power switch had been accidentally turned off. The cooler was turned on and reached 41F during today’s visit. Since the items were discarded and the cooler is operational, this violation is considered corrected-on-site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation
Inspector observed the following areas to need a deep-cleaning:
1. Flooring in kitchen under all shelving and equipment.
Ensure these areas are kept clean to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: The inspector observed pests present in the kitchen, dish area, and bar spaces. The insects were observed present on glue traps in all three spaces. The PIC informed the inspector that active pest control measures are being taken. Pest control is currently visiting the facility every two weeks. The inspector recommends writing dates on all glue traps for monitoring purposes, sealing all holes and coving to prevent pest movement, and deep cleaning the floors and equipment to starve out pests. The inspector will spot check the facility to confirm pest reduction in the 30 days (2/17/2026 to avoid weekend and holiday). Ensure receipts of pest control visits are kept in the facility for the inspector to view.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following areas to need a deep-cleaning:
1. Flooring in kitchen under all shelving and equipment.
2. Flooring in dish area.

Ensure these areas are kept clean to prevent cross-contamination and to limit the presence of pests in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the coving in the kitchen space to be damaged and separating from the wall. There were also two holes in the wall next to the kitchen hand sink and on the ceiling next to the walk-in cooler. Ensure these areas are in good repair and properly repaired to prevent the movement of pests in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above the safe maximum cold holding temperature in the 2-door cooler:
1. Cottage cheese
2. Sour cream
3. Coleslaw
4. Tavern cheese
5. Cut lettuce
6. Cut tomato
7. Caesar dressing
8. Ranch dressing
9. Shredded cheese

These items all measured roughly 50-60 degrees with the infrared thermometer. The digital thermometer for the cooler read 43F. The PIC was informed and chose to discard all TCS foods in the cooler. The PIC called and scheduled maintenance on the cooler. Since the items were discarded, this violation is considered corrected-on-site.

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed RTE eat foods (sour cream, cottage cheese) to be dated according to expiration date on original packaging. Advised PIC that RTE foods transferred into new packaging must be dated to reflect 7 days following the opening of the original container. Due to the failure of the cooler, these items were voluntarily discarded. Education was conducted with the PIC regarding proper date marking procedure and a handout was provided.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The 2-door standing cooler was observed to measure 50-60F with the infrared probe. The interior of the cooler was not cold to the touch. The PIC was informed and determined that the cooler was not operational. Maintenance on the cooler was scheduled during the inspection. A follow-up will be conducted on 6/20/2025 to ensure the cooler has been repaired. In the meantime, the 2-door standing cooler cannot be used to store TCS foods. The walk-in will be used until the service is completed.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

1) Raw fish is observed over RTE sauce cups in the walk in cooler. 2) Raw bacon is observed over raw tomatoes in the walk in cooler. The PIC was consulted and moved the items during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food items are stored based on their cooking temperatures in the coolers.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

Multiple utensils and pans in the dish room have been washed and put up without being completely cleaned. Food debris is still observed on each of them. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean these items again and to ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage. All items were moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Observed RTE eat foods (sour cream, cottage cheese) to be dated according to expiration date on original packaging. Advised PIC that RTE foods transferred into new packaging must be dated to reflect 7 days following the opening of the original container. Dates were adjusted during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Observed cloths in-use for wiping food contact surfaces stored moist and on prep tables. Advised PIC that cloths must be stored in their sanitizer buckets between uses. This ensures that the cloth is clean and without potential contamination before each use. Cook staff placed in-use cloths to their sanitizer buckets during inspection.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Observed single-use utensils to be stored in metal tubs which were contaminated with dust and food debris. Observed single-use condiment cups to be stored with food contact surfaces exposed or without adequate coverings to protect from dust/debris contamination. Observed large sharpies to be in a container with plastic spoons. Advised PIC to keep containers holding single-use utensils clean and to keep single-use food contact surfaces covered or inverted on a clean surface such as the bottom of a container or clean work surface. Containers holding single-use utensils were washed and contaminated utensils were disposed of during inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Observed shelf of kitchen pass-through to be damaged (cleanable coating lifting from wood shelf). Observed 3-part sink in dishwashing room to have gaps between the sink and wall. Advised PIC to fix these areas such that the surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. Any gaps/cracks/crevices on surfaces can harbor bacteria and other pathogens.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed several employees put on new gloves and begin to prepare food without first washing hands. Wash hands anytime new gloves are worn. Discussed proper hand washing technique and glove use with PIC. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed box of tubes of ground beef to be stored directly on floor in back room walk in cooler. Box was placed on shelf during inspection. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1) Observed blade of counter-mounted can opener to be soiled with food debris. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during inspection. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
